name: Zoetis Inc.

profile.description: Zoetis discovers, develops, manufactures, and commercializes medicines, vaccines, diagnostics, and biodevices for companion animals and livestock. Spun off from Pfizer in 2013, it is the world's largest animal health company, with FY2025 revenue of $9.47B. Key franchises include Simparica Trio parasiticides, Apoquel and Cytopoint dermatology, the Librela and Solensia monoclonal antibody pain treatments, and the AI-powered Vetscan Imagyst diagnostics platform. In August 2026 Zoetis cut FY2026 guidance to $9.12-$9.32B revenue (organic operational growth of -3% to -1%) amid weaker U.S. companion animal demand and intensifying competition.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Zoetis pioneered monoclonal antibody pain therapy for pets with Librela and Solensia and built a point-of-care diagnostics business, opening significant new revenue streams; however, Librela sales slowed after a February 2025 label update on neurological adverse events [3]. AI Deployment (2/2): Zoetis ships AI to veterinarians through Vetscan Imagyst, with seven AI testing applications including AI dermatology, urine sediment, AI Masses (2025) and the AI-powered Vetscan OptiCell hematology analyzer, and it agreed in July 2026 to acquire AI-assisted radiology firm VitalRADS [4]. Market Share (1/2): Zoetis remains the largest animal health company by revenue, but it is losing share in parasiticides, dermatology and OA pain, which helped drive Q1 and Q2 2026 revenue misses [1][3]. Pipeline (1/2): Diagnostics and biologics expansion continues, but no named next-gen blockbuster with a launch date and revenue visibility was found [1][4]. R&D Intensity (1/1): R&D of $698M was 7.4% of FY2025 revenue, at or above animal-health peers [5].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Zoetis' purpose, 'to nurture our world and humankind by advancing care for animals', is specific and thoughtful and ties animal health to food security and the human-animal bond; it has been consistently articulated since the 2013 spin-off. Community Impact (1/2): Zoetis runs its Driven to Care sustainability and veterinary community programs, but distinctive dollar-quantified community investment was not found. Employee Retention (0/2): No turnover or tenure data was found after searching. Insider Buying (1/2): FMP insider statistics show three open-market purchases in Q2 2026 and two sales in Q1 2026, with most other activity being equity awards, so buying and selling are roughly balanced [6].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on the Dividend weighting (12 weight units). Profitability is exceptional: ROE of 64.9%, a 27.7% profit margin and a forward P/E of 12.4x all score full marks, and the dividend is a standout with a 33.9% payout ratio, 13 consecutive years paid and grown since the 2013 IPO, and a 20.1% five-year dividend CAGR ($0.80 in 2020 to $2.00 in 2025) [5]. The main drag is D/E of 294%, close to the 300% floor after a 41% rise in debt during 2025 alongside buybacks; revenue is flat (-0.2% YoY) and the five-year revenue CAGR is 7.2% ($6.68B to $9.47B) [1][5]. Weighted 10.50/12 = 8.75, rounded to 9; liquidity is ~$397M per day.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Zoetis makes physical biologics, vaccines, parasiticides and diagnostic instruments under FDA/USDA regulation and sells them through veterinarians and livestock producers, so AI has no path to substitute its products. Its headwinds in 2026 come from competitors and weaker clinic visits, not AI [1][3]. AI is in fact embedded in Zoetis' own diagnostics, where Vetscan Imagyst runs seven AI applications [4]. AI Opportunity (0/1): Zoetis does not disclose separate revenue for its AI diagnostics, so no quantifiable AI revenue can be cited.

infinite_game.summary: Zoetis has a genuine cause in advancing care for animals and has reinvested in biologics and AI diagnostics. Through Sinek's lens, though, it is a company still being tested: the Librela adverse-event controversy, a pending securities class action, two guidance cuts in 2026 and a debt-funded buyback push suggest finite pressures are rising.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): 'Nurture our world and humankind by advancing care for animals' is distinctive and service-oriented, and investments in first-in-class pet biologics and veterinary diagnostics trace back to it [4]. It has not yet been validated by multi-decade consistency or a leadership transition, and it is now being tested by the 2026 downturn [1].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): CEO Kristin Peck, a Pfizer veteran who has led Zoetis since January 2020, has provided leadership continuity, and McKinsey profiled how she empowered employees during the pandemic [2]. No turnover data was found to establish exceptional trust, and the pressure from the 2026 guidance cuts is a test ahead.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Commentary on the 2026 results centers on defending share against competitors in parasiticides, dermatology and OA pain; no evidence was found of management framing rivals as a source of learning [1][3].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Zoetis has extended beyond pharmaceuticals into monoclonal antibodies, point-of-care AI diagnostics and, via VitalRADS, virtual radiology [4]. These are meaningful adjacent moves rather than a reinvention of the business.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Zoetis kept R&D near $700M (7.4% of revenue) and continued diagnostics M&A through the downturn [4][5]. Against that, debt rose 41% in 2025 while share count fell 2.4%, and a class action alleges management hid slowing Librela sales, which points to quarter-focused behavior [3][5].

investment_thesis: Zoetis is the world's largest animal health company, earning a 27.7% net margin and 64.9% ROE on $9.5B of revenue, yet it trades at just 12.4x forward earnings with a 2.66% yield and a dividend that has grown 20% a year over five years [5]. Q2 2026 still produced $691M of net income ($1.65 per share) despite the downturn, and its AI-powered Vetscan Imagyst diagnostics platform, now expanding into radiology via VitalRADS, adds a recurring, technology-led growth leg [1][4].
thesis_continued: The bear case is a franchise under competitive siege: FY2026 guidance was cut to -3% to -1% organic operational growth and adjusted EPS of $6.15-$6.25 after misses in Q1 and Q2, with share losses in Simparica Trio, Apoquel/Cytopoint and Librela [1][3]. Leverage has risen to 294% D/E, and a securities class action (City of Ann Arbor v. Zoetis, S.D.N.Y.) over Librela disclosures remains pending, adding legal and reputational overhang [3][5].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results (early November) showing stabilization in U.S. companion animal clinic visits after Q2's 1% organic operational decline
Growth of the AI diagnostics platform (seven Vetscan Imagyst applications plus VitalRADS radiology) as a new recurring revenue stream
A 13th consecutive dividend increase from the current $2.12 annual rate, supported by a 33.9% payout ratio
key_risks: Continued share loss in parasiticides, dermatology and OA pain to Elanco and other entrants, extending the 2026 revenue decline
Librela neurological adverse-event label update and the pending securities class action eroding veterinarian trust
D/E near 294% after a 41% debt increase in 2025 limits balance-sheet flexibility if the downturn persists
